subtitle: Beef & vegetable soup
verso: Beef soup with its bone: taste it once and you'll keep coming home.
story: The everyday soup of every Mexican home: beef shank with the bone and marrow, corn on the cob and whatever vegetables the market has. The rice goes in the bowl, not the pot.

ingredients.title: The meat
items: 3 lb beef shank (chambarete), bone-in with marrow
1 lb beef short ribs (costilla de res), optional

ingredients.title: The vegetables
items: 3 ears of corn, each cut in 3 rounds
1 chayote, peeled and cut in wedges

steps: Put the meat, onion and garlic in a big pot with the water. Bring to a boil and skim the foam for 15 minutes.
Add the salt, lower the heat and simmer partly covered 2 hours, until the meat is tender.
Blend the tomatoes with a cup of broth and strain into the pot. It gives the caldo a light color.
Add the vegetables by how long they take: corn and carrots first, 15 minutes; then potatoes and chayote, 10 minutes; then zucchini and cabbage, 8 minutes.
Turn off the heat and drop in the cilantro and mint. Taste for salt.
Put a spoon of arroz rojo in each bowl, add meat and vegetables, and ladle the broth over. Lime and chile at the table.

pressureCooker.time: 40 min high pressure + 15 min natural release
steps: Put the meat, onion, garlic, salt and [[3 quarts]] water in the pot. High pressure 40 minutes, natural release 15.
Add the strained tomato, corn, carrots, potatoes and chayote. High pressure 3 minutes, quick release.
Switch to Sauté, add the zucchini and cabbage, and simmer 5 minutes. Add the cilantro and mint off the heat.

tips: Scoop the marrow out of the bone onto a hot tortilla with salt and salsa. That's the cook's reward.
Mint is the quiet secret in a lot of family caldos. One sprig is enough.

variations.name: Mole de Olla
variations.subtitle: Chile-red beef soup with xoconostle
variations.note: Caldo de res's spicier cousin. The broth is tinted with dried chiles and soured with xoconostle, a tart cactus fruit. Many central families drop in chochoyotes, little masa-and-epazote dumplings pressed with a thumb, for the last 10 minutes. The saying «¡A darle, que es mole de olla!» means let's get to it.

items: Meat and broth from the base, steps 1–2
4 chiles guajillo, 2 chiles pasilla (1 ancho, optional)
2 Roma tomatoes, 2 garlic cloves, ¼ onion
2 xoconostles, peeled, seeded and quartered (or the juice of 1 lime at the end)

steps: Cook the meat as in the base.
Toast and soak the chiles. Blend with the tomatoes, garlic and onion, strain, and fry in the lard 5 minutes.
Add the chile to the broth with the corn, potatoes, chayote and xoconostle. Cook 15 minutes.
Add the green beans, zucchini and epazote and cook 8 minutes more.
Serve with chopped onion, serrano and lime.
variations.pressureNote: Same pressure steps as the base. Add the fried chile with the first batch of vegetables.
